We start by showing that the seminorm of the coefficients of the slice function \( f(p, \cdot) \) is bounded by a specific expression. Specifically, we use the theorem that for a smooth and periodic function \( f \) on the torus, the seminorm of its coefficients is bounded by a constant involving the seminorm of the function and the sum of the inverse weights of the frequencies. This gives us:
\[
\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} \text{weight}(k)^{w.length + 1} \cdot \| \text{coefficient}(f(p, \cdot), k) \| \leq (3^{w.length + 5} \cdot C) \cdot \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} \text{weight}(k)^{-4}
\]

Next, we use the theorem that the norm of the derivative word of the inverse function is bounded by a constant involving the norm of the inverse coefficients and the length of the derivative word. This gives us:
\[
\| \text{derivativeWord}(w, \text{slice}(\text{inverse}(d, f), p)) Y \| \leq (6 \cdot \|\omega^{-1}\| \cdot \|\omega\|^{w.length}) \cdot \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} \text{weight}(k)^{w.length + 1} \cdot \| \text{coefficient}(f(p, \cdot), k) \|
\]

Using the bound on the seminorm of the coefficients, we can further bound the norm of the derivative word:
\[
(6 \cdot \|\omega^{-1}\| \cdot \|\omega\|^{w.length}) \cdot \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} \text{weight}(k)^{w.length + 1} \cdot \| \text{coefficient}(f(p, \cdot), k) \| \leq (6 \cdot \|\omega^{-1}\| \cdot \|\omega\|^{w.length}) \cdot (3^{w.length + 5} \cdot C) \cdot \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} \text{weight}(k)^{-4}
\]

Finally, we simplify the expression using the definition of the mixed loss constant and the properties of exponents and multiplication:
\[
(6 \cdot \|\omega^{-1}\| \cdot \|\omega\|^{w.length}) \cdot (3^{w.length + 5} \cdot C) \cdot \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} \text{weight}(k)^{-4} = \text{mixedLossConstant}(w.length) \cdot C
\]

Thus, we have:
\[
\| \text{derivativeWord}(w, \text{slice}(\text{inverse}(d, f), p)) Y \| \leq \text{mixedLossConstant}(w.length) \cdot C
\]

This completes the proof. \(\blacksquare\)
